config.title: Controlled Input

intro.title: Controlled Input
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form with an input field that displays and updates text as the user types. You'll learn about controlled inputs in React, where the component's state directly manages the input's value, creating a single source of truth for form data. This concept involves using React's useState hook to store the input value and an onChange event handler to update the state whenever the user types. You'll work with JSX to create the input element and connect it to your component's state using the value and onChange props. By the end of this lesson, you'll understand how React components can control form inputs and respond to user interactions in real-time.
intro.usecase: Controlled inputs are fundamental to any interactive web application where users need to input data. You'll find them powering login forms, search bars, comment sections, and checkout processes across platforms like Amazon, Facebook, and Google. E-commerce sites use controlled inputs for product filters and quantity selectors, while dashboard applications rely on them for data entry forms and real-time search functionality. Social media platforms implement controlled inputs for post creation, messaging, and profile updates, ensuring immediate validation and dynamic user feedback. As a React developer, mastering controlled inputs is essential since they form the backbone of user interaction in modern web applications.

objectives: Implement state variables to control input field values
Bind input elements to React state using the value prop
Configure onChange event handlers to update input state
Construct controlled form components that manage their own data
Apply two-way data binding between input fields and component state
Manipulate input behavior by controlling when and how values change
Initialize controlled inputs with default values from state

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from 'react' to enable component creation and state management for the controlled input.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook from the 'react' library. Both will be needed for creating a component with state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing multiple items from a library
import { Component, render } from 'react-dom';
steps.expectedOutcome: React and useState are imported from 'react', setting up the foundation for creating a controlled input component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react' in a single import statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both React and useState from 'react' using the import statement. Both are needed for this lesson.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ControlledInput
steps.hint: Define a component using either function declaration or arrow function syntax. The component should be named ControlledInput.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create your ControlledInput component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named ControlledInput is created
successCriteria: ControlledInput component is defined as a function
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your component is named exactly 'ControlledInput' and is defined as a function.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a functional component. You can use either 'function ControlledInput() {}' or 'const ControlledInput = () => {}' syntax.

steps.title: Initialize state for input value
steps.instruction: Inside the ControlledInput component, initialize state by creating a state variable named 'inputValue' with an initial value of an empty string using useState.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook with an empty string as the initial value. Destructure the result to get both the state variable and its setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: initializing state with useState
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'inputValue' initialized to an empty string, along with its corresponding setter function.
successCriteria: inputValue state is initialized using useState with an empty string as the initial value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start with useState! Make sure you're naming the state variable 'inputValue' and initializing it with an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: use the useState hook to create a state variable called 'inputValue' with an initial value of an empty string ('').

steps.title: Define change handler function
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleInputChange that takes an event parameter and updates the inputValue state with the new input value from the event target
steps.hint: Use event.target.value to get the current input value and pass it to the setInputValue function
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleInputChange function is created that accepts an event parameter and calls setInputValue with event.target.value
successCriteria: handleInputChange function is defined and uses event.target.value to update inputValue state
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your function takes an event parameter and uses event.target.value to get the input's current value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The change handler function should accept an event parameter and call setInputValue with event.target.value to update the state.

steps.title: Add JSX return structure
steps.instruction: Update the return statement to include a heading that says 'Controlled Input Demo' inside the div container.
steps.hint: Add an h1 or h2 element with the text 'Controlled Input Demo' between the opening and closing div tags.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns JSX with a div container that includes a heading displaying 'Controlled Input Demo'.
successCriteria: A heading element (h1, h2, etc.) with the text 'Controlled Input Demo' is present inside the div in the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your heading displays 'Controlled Input Demo' and is inside the div container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading should be placed inside the div container in the return statement. Use an h1 or h2 element with the text 'Controlled Input Demo'.

steps.title: Add input element with controlled properties
steps.instruction: Add an input element with value prop set to inputValue and onChange prop set to handleInputChange.
steps.hint: The input should have two key props: value={inputValue} to control its value, and onChange={handleInputChange} to handle changes.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: controlled input with value and onChange
<input value={userText} onChange={handleTextChange} />
steps.expectedOutcome: An input element is added inside the div with value prop connected to inputValue state and onChange prop connected to handleInputChange function.
successCriteria: Input element has value prop set to inputValue and onChange prop set to handleInputChange
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your input has both value={inputValue} and onChange={handleInputChange} props.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input needs to be controlled with value={inputValue} and onChange={handleInputChange} props to connect it to your state.

steps.title: Display current input value
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element below the input that displays the current inputValue state
steps.hint: Use JSX curly braces to display the inputValue variable inside a paragraph element
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: displaying a variable in JSX

{userName}
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element that shows the current value of the input field, demonstrating the controlled input behavior
successCriteria: A paragraph element displays the inputValue state using JSX curly braces
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the paragraph uses JSX curly braces to display the inputValue variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph should display the inputValue state. Use curly braces {} to embed the variable in JSX.

steps.title: Add clear button
steps.instruction: Add a button element after the input that clears the input value when clicked
steps.hint: Create a button with onClick that calls a function to set inputValue to an empty string
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: button that resets a counter
<button onClick={() => setCount(0)}>Reset</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button appears that, when clicked, clears the input field by setting the state to an empty string
successCriteria: Button element is added with onClick handler that calls setInputValue with empty string
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your button has an onClick handler that sets inputValue to an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button needs an onClick handler that calls setInputValue('') to clear the input.

steps.title: Export the component
steps.instruction: Add an export default statement to make the ControlledInput component available for import in other files.
steps.hint: Use 'export default' followed by the component name. This should be placed at the end of the file.
steps.analogousExample:
// Making a component available for import
export default MyComponent;
steps.expectedOutcome: The ControlledInput component is exported as the default export, making it available for import in other files.
successCriteria: The component is exported using export default ControlledInput statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with exporting. Make sure you're using 'export default' followed by the component name 'ControlledInput'.
steps.feedbackWrong: use 'export default ControlledInput;' to make the component available for import in other files. This statement should be added after the component definition.

steps.title: Test the controlled input behavior
steps.instruction: Add the export default statement for the ControlledInput component to complete the controlled input implementation
steps.hint: Use 'export default' followed by the component name to make it available for import in other files
steps.analogousExample:
// Exporting a component for use elsewhere
export default MyComponent;
steps.expectedOutcome: The ControlledInput component is exported as the default export, making it ready to be imported and used in other components or applications
successCriteria: The export default statement is added for the ControlledInput component
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure to export the ControlledInput component using 'export default ControlledInput;'
steps.feedbackWrong: add the export statement. Use 'export default' followed by your component name to make it available for import.
